subject: Clarifying EU-only split-processing & transfer controls
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@eurobank.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Sofia Lindström <sofia.lindstrom@dataprotec.se>
Date: Mon, 10 Apr 2028 09:15:00 +0100
Subject: EU-only processing — technical and contractual evidence needed

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we move into procurement, legal has asked for a clear description of how Redwood will ensure EU-only processing for our regulated workloads. In particular they want answers to:

- Can you guarantee that customer data and model inputs/outputs are processed and stored only within EU regions (no backups, replicas, or logs outside EU)?
- What technical controls (KMS, network isolation, region scoping) do you offer as evidence?
- Do you implement any split-processing/pseudonymization patterns that reduce the need for data transfers?
- How do you combine SCCs with technical measures (if SCCs are still the chosen legal basis) — what evidence can you provide to procurement?

We need something we can attach to our procurement pack (architecture diagram + checklist + short attestation). Can you share a draft by EOD Wednesday?

Oliver
Head of Cloud Risk — EuroBank

---
Attachment: request-scope-eurobank.pdf (application/pdf)

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@eurobank.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Apr 2028 13:42:00 +0100
Subject: Re: EU-only processing — technical and contractual evidence needed

Oliver — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Laura (legal) and Markus (infra) so we can cover legal + technical evidence. High level answers below; we'll follow up with a short packet (diagram + checklist + attestation draft) by EOD Wednesday.

Quick answers:
1) EU-only processing guarantee: we offer an \"EU-only\" hosting mode for Dedicated and Private deployments where all compute, persistent storage, and KV caches are provisioned in customer-selected EU regions. For Hosted customers we also support region pinning with strong routing rules and no outbound replication by default. We can provide an affidavit & infra config snapshot showing active resources in eu-west-1 for the tenant.

2) Technical controls: regional VPCs, customer KMS (optional BYOK) with keys in EU KMS tenancy, network egress filters, encrypted at-rest and in-transit, and auditing logs scoped to the region. We also support HSM-backed key stores for Private deployments.

3) Split-processing/pseudonymization: we provide an optional split-processing architecture: tokenization/pseudonymization happens in-region (EU) before any model artifact or minimalized token set leaves the region. For additional assurance we support an in-region transformer inference variant so the entire inference pipeline can remain in-EU.

4) SCCs + technical measures: our standard approach is SCCs + documented supplementary technical measures (region controls, pseudonymization, contractual restrictions on subprocessors). Laura will add legal detail below.

Attachments I will circulate in the packet: redwood-eu-data-flow-diagram.pdf, redwood-supplementary-measures-checklist.xlsx, redwood-eu-attestation-draft.docx

Next steps: Laura to confirm wording for attestation; Markus to provide a scrubbed infra snapshot and network flow diagram.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
+44 20 7946 0923

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@eurobank.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 10:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: EU-only processing — legal framing and SCCs approach

Oliver — quick legal framing from our side.

- We treat Schrems II / EDPB guidance seriously: for transfers to third countries we propose SCCs plus targeted supplementary measures (technical + contractual). If EuroBank requires avoidance of transfers entirely, our Dedicated/Private offerings allow you to keep processing in-EU with no cross-border replicas.

- SCCs: we can sign the EU SCCs (controller-processor modules where applicable) and include a schedule of subprocessors limited to EU regions. Procurement typically asks for: signed SCCs, a subprocessor list, evidence of in-region KMS, and the region-scoped logging policy. We can provide all four.

- Supplementary measures we can document and evidence:
  * Technical: BYOK in EU, encryption in transit & at rest, tokenization/pseudonymization in-region, no remote debugging endpoints that exfiltrate logs outside region, restricted administrative access from IPs within EU or via VPN/GW.
  * Organizational: limited admin roles, documented access reviews, SOC2 + available customer audit options for Private.

We will produce language for a short attestation stating: \"Redwood Inference will process EuroBank data only within the EU region(s) specified in the agreement; backups and logs are stored only in those regions; cryptographic keys are resident in EU KMS unless BYOK provided otherwise.\" Please review and tell us if you need stronger or more specific language.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@eurobank.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 14:28:00 +0100
Subject: Re: EU-only processing — technical packet and infra evidence

Oliver — attaching a scrubbed infra snapshot and notes (see links below). A couple of implementation points to call out:

- No cross-region replicas: for the Dedicated mode assigned to EuroBank we will disable asynchronous replication and object-versioning to any non-EU bucket. Snapshots are taken to a lifecycle within the same region.
- KV cache policy: we have in-region KV caches with TTLs controlled by the customer; by default the KV cache does not export to analytics pipelines outside the region.
- Telemetry and logs: we can provide region-scoped log exports and an export manifest showing only eu-west-1 endpoints.
- Split-processing option: tokenization service running in the EU will emit opaque tokens; model execution can be done in the same region or in an isolated Private cluster if you want zero risk of egress.

Links:
- Diagram (scrubbed): https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/redwood-eu-data-flow-diagram.pdf
- Supplementary checklist: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/redwood-supplementary-measures-checklist.xlsx

I'll also prepare a short infra snapshot (redacted) we can hand to procurement that lists active VPC IDs and KMS key ARNs. Priyom, can we include a one-page runbook for evidence collection for procurement?

-Markus
Director, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@eurobank.com>

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: EU-only processing — technical and contractual evidence needed

Thanks team — this is exactly in line with what procurement wanted. A few quick asks before we close the RFC:

1) Can you provide the draft attestation as a single PDF we can append to the contract?
2) Procurement would like the scrubbed infra snapshot and a single contact for any follow-up audit requests (name + email).
3) For the split-processing option: can you confirm any extra latency or functional changes (e.g., tokenization affecting prompt context length)? We need that for the SRE team review.

If you can get 1+2 to us by tomorrow morning UK time, procurement will be able to move to signatures.

Oliver
